feed.title: NPR Topics: National
feed.subtitle: Follow NPR National News for reporting across the United States. Explore coverage of economic affordability, immigration, climate, environmental policy, justice and social trends.

entry.title: Democrats won big on issues like immigration. But ICE still has the money
entry.summary: Following Tuesday's "blue wave," Democrats have vowed to reign in ICE's power. What could they actually accomplish?

entry.title: On wild Cumberland Island, a land swap proposal stirs controversy
entry.summary: Visitors, ecologists, park rangers and residents all love this wild barrier island off the coast of southern Georgia. But they have different ideas of how to best protect it.

entry.title: Democrats won big. Can they lower your grocery bill?
entry.summary: Affordability concerns were top of mind for voters heading into the midterms, as tariffs and the war in Iran drove up prices, including food costs. Now, Americans are expecting relief from Washington.

entry.title: Nvidia launches investigation into CEO's alleged relationship with Chinese spy
entry.summary: The chipmaking giant says it is looking into reports by The New York Times that its CEO, Jensen Huang, was the target of a Chinese intelligence operation.

entry.title: NASA is looking for astronauts to live and work on the Moon
entry.summary: NASA needs more recruits in order to return to the moon after being gone more than half a century.

entry.title: This podcast explores why things made by hand are so special
entry.summary: NPR's Rob Schmitz speaks with Sam Dingman, host of The Analogs podcast from NPR member station KJZZ.

entry.title: SS United States, a historic ship will be sunk to create an artificial reef
entry.summary: NPR's Ayesha Rascoe talks to Alex Fogg, Natural Resources Chief of Okaloosa County, Florida, about efforts to deliberately sink the SS United States and create an artificial reef in its wreckage.

entry.title: Homelessness in the U.S. dropped again. HUD and housing advocates differ on why
entry.summary: Homelessness in the U.S. has dropped for the second year in a row, two analyses found. But the Trump administration and homeless advocates credit different reasons for the decline.

entry.title: Climate change is altering the colors we see in the world: an illustrated journey
entry.summary: From Arctic landscapes to insect bodies, climate change is shifting the familiar colors of nature.

entry.title: One air ambulance service rethinks what it takes to practice medicine in the sky
entry.summary: Air medical service comes with high risks, high costs, and staffing struggles. To reduce turnover and serve rural patients, LifeFlight of Maine is putting the needs of healthcare workers first.
